plan: Given my value of $9, I should bid just below or at my value to maximize profit. Bidding above $9 risks paying more than the prize's worth, resulting in a loss. Since rational bidders bid close to their value, I'll bid slightly less than $9 to avoid overpaying. This strategy maximizes expected profit by winning only when the second-highest bid is lower than my value, ensuring a positive net gain.

My value for the prize is $20. To maximize profit, bid slightly below my value to ensure a profit if I win. Since all bidders are rational, they will also bid close to their values. Thus, I should bid slightly below $20 to avoid overbidding and ensure a small profit margin if I win. A bid of $19.9 is reasonable, as it is close to my value but leaves room for a profit.

Given my value of $20, I'll aim to bid slightly below it to maximize profit if I win. Rational bidders will bid below their value to avoid negative profit. Assuming others bid close to their values, I'll bid $19.9 to outbid those valuing slightly less than me, while still securing positive profit.
